lines: What if you built a real AI app in your very first module?
This is AI 410.
Before the lecture, you watch it work.
A guided simulator shows how an AI agent calls a tool, one step at a time.
No account. No code.
Then you break it on purpose.
Take the tool away, and the model still answers: confidently, and wrong.
No error. Nothing crashes.
That's when you learn the skill that matters most: catching AI when it's wrong.
Next, you build it for real in GitHub Codespaces.
An AI assistant helps you get a working app fast.
Everything runs on free tools, with no credit card.
But the AI's draft isn't the finish line.
You explain how it works in your own words, then extend it by hand, without AI.
And when something's confusing, you tell your instructor exactly where you got stuck.
By the end of the term, you combine everything into an app of your own.
Like this example: a flashcard coach that turns your notes into study cards, on your phone.
Every card comes from your own documents.
AI 410: AI Engineering.
Part of the BS in AI at City University of Seattle.
See the course at the link on screen.
